senses.definition: Primary; most important; first level in importance.
senses.example: Smith is the principal architect of this design.

senses.definition: Of or relating to a prince; princely.
senses.example: But walkt at will, and wandred to and fro, / In the pride of his freedome principall.

senses.definition: Chosen or assumed among a branch of possible values of a multi-valued function so that the function is single-valued.
senses.example: Two is the principal square root of 4. Both −2 and +2 are square roots of 4.

senses.definition: The money originally invested or loaned, on which basis interest and returns are calculated.
senses.example: A portion of your mortgage payment goes to reduce the principal, and the rest covers interest.

senses.definition: The chief administrator of a school.
senses.example: The important administrative figure to the teacher is the school principal.
senses.register: Australia, Canada, New-Zealand, Philippines, US, countable, uncountable

senses.definition: The chief executive and chief academic officer of a university or college.
senses.example:

senses.definition: A legal person that authorizes another (the agent) to act on their behalf; or on whose behalf an agent or gestor in a negotiorum gestio acts.
senses.example: When an attorney represents a client, the client is the principal who permits the attorney, the client′s agent, to act on the client′s behalf.

senses.definition: The primary participant in a crime.
senses.example: The accessories may be prosecuted, tried and punished, though the principal has not been prosecuted or has been acquitted.

senses.definition: A partner or owner of a business.
A type of stop on a pipe organ consisting of flue pipes with a bright tonal quality. They are also sometimes referred to as a diapason.
The construction that gives shape and strength to a roof, generally a truss of timber or iron; or, loosely, the most important member of a piece of framing.
The first two long feathers of a hawk's wing.

senses.definition: One of the turrets or pinnacles of waxwork and tapers with which the posts and centre of a funeral hearse were formerly crowned
An essential point or rule; a principle.
senses.example: Set two classes of monitors to question each other; so that one may try to outquestion the other. Explain to them the principal of every subject they have to teach.

senses.definition: A dancer at the highest rank within a professional dance company, particularly a ballet company.
A main character or lead actor.
